subject: Post-call: FinSecure deployment checklist, control-plane/networking questions
body:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex@finsecure.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: FinSecure deployment checklist, control-plane/networking questions

Alex / Priya — thanks again for a productive discovery call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical PoC: 

Summary from our call
- FinSecure's goals: deploy an inference stack for document analysis inside your VPC (no egress), meet SOC2/audit evidence requirements, and keep median token latency under 120ms for line-of-business models.
- Primary constraints: network isolation (air-gap or strict egress controls), KMS/HSM integration for key management, and procurement timeline targeting an August POC start.
- Competitive context you mentioned: evaluating hyperscaler managed endpoints (private link / VPC endpoints) and one other inference API vendor with a hybrid offering.

What we propose (high level)
1) Private control-plane option: we can host a private control plane in your AWS account (VPC peering or managed VPC subnet) or deliver an on-prem package if air-gap is required. Control plane responsibilities: model lifecycle, rollouts, observability hooks — optional to keep in-scope.
2) Data path: inference traffic keeps model execution inside your VPC on Dedicated nodes; control plane traffic can be routed either via a customer-managed NAT (no persistent storage of payloads) or through a private peering link.
3) Security/compliance: KMS/HSM integration supported (we use envelope encryption patterns), audit logs for every request, and optional log-forwarding to your SIEM.

Requested follow-ups (actions)
- From FinSecure: network diagram showing where you'd like the runtime placed and an internal contact for your security/infra team (if different from Priya).
- From Redwood: short checklist for tests we recommend during PoC (connectivity checks, latency profiles, prefix/KV cache verification, and a short traceroute/tcpdump plan). See attached redwood-poc-checklist.pdf and networking-questions-table.xlsx.
- Procurement: we'll circulate a preliminary SOW and pricing snapshot (attached initial-sow-template.docx) and can scope a 4-week PoC.

Parallel competitive notes (from our side)
- Hyperscaler managed endpoints: reasonable for quick start but often rely on a centralized control plane and can introduce egress that violates your requirements unless you subscribe to VPC endpoint/private link options; those can add unpredictable costs and require complex routing.
- Other inference APIs: some vendors offer edge appliances but limit model variants or lack unified rollout/observability. Redwood differentiator: same runtime across hosted/dedicated/private with opt-in private control plane and explicit KMS/HSM integrations.

Proposed next steps
1) Alex / Priya: share the network diagram and security contact by EOD Thu (16 Jul).
2) Redwood: Naomi and Rishi to provide a short tech note on control-plane options and a minimal connectivity test plan by Thu.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up to align scope and procurement milestones — propose Fri 17 Jul or Mon 20 Jul.

Thanks — Olga

--
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinSecure deployment checklist, control-plane/networking questions

Thanks Olga — helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from our infra/security teams before we hand off the diagram: 

1) Air-gapped feasibility: can Redwood run the entire control plane and runtime on-prem behind our firewall with zero outbound connectivity? If not fully air-gapped, what minimal outbound endpoints (domains/IPs) would need to be allowed and for what frequency?
2) KMS/HSM: we plan to use our existing AWS KMS + CloudHSM. Will Redwood support customer-managed CMKs and HSM-backed keys for model decryption and key wrapping?
3) Network path: if we keep a private control plane in our AWS account, what IP ranges will you use for management traffic? We prefer whitelisting a small set of CIDRs rather than broad VPC peering.
4) Latency guarantees: you mentioned 120ms median — can you provide a latency profile from similar customers inside AWS private deployments (p95/p99) and what tuning steps are typical?

Also looping Eric from our partner team — he asked whether marketplace-managed images (e.g., an AMI you publish) are an option to speed POC deployment.

Alex

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Monroe <alex@finsecure.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 07:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: FinSecure deployment checklist, control-plane/networking questions

Alex / Priya — answering each question with proposed testable steps. I'm the lead on network/control-plane integration for private deployments.

1) Air-gapped feasibility- Short answer: full air-gap (zero outbound) is viable if you accept an on-prem package for the control plane and runtime image pre-baked; this is the path others have taken. Trade-offs: updates and model onboarding are manual via secure media or a controlled sync window.
- What we need from you: scope of allowed physical media/process and a maintenance plan (we'll capture in the SOW).

2) Minimal outbound for managed private control plane- If you prefer Redwood-hosted control plane but isolated networking, the minimal outbound is for health-checks and control-plane RPCs (our control plane uses a small set of domains and certificate pinning). Typical traffic: TLS to control.redwood-inference.com on 443 for control signals and periodic certificate/heartbeat checks. We can provide exact FQDNs and IP ranges for whitelisting once we determine region and whether you want dedicated IP ranges.

3) KMS/HSM integration- We support customer-managed CMKs and HSM-backed keys via AWS KMS and CloudHSM for envelope encryption. We never persist plaintext keys; we store only encrypted key material. For the PoC: we can demonstrate key wrapping with your CMK and provide a test script to validate.

4) Network path and CIDR requests- For a private control plane in your account we recommend either (a) a dedicated /27 for management endpoints or (b) a set of static Elastic IPs if you prefer NAT-based routing. We'll avoid broad VPC peering if you want strict whitelisting. We will provide the exact ranges in the tech note.

5) Latency profiles and tuning steps- Example from a finance customer running in-VPC Dedicated nodes: median 95ms, p95 180ms (sustained small requests), with caching and batching tuned p95 dropped to ~140ms. Typical levers: model quantization, longer pre-filling of KV cache for chat workflows, and thin-client batching at the SDK layer. We'll provide a short tuning guide with recommended batch sizes for your 120ms median target.

Proposed PoC tests (minimal set we can start with)
- Connectivity smoke: whitelisted IPs/FQDN resolution, TLS handshake, and simple GET/POST to health endpoints.
- Latency baseline: synthetic token-only tests from a low-latency EC2 instance in your subnet to measure median/p95/p99.
- Security validation: KMS envelope wrap demo, sample audit log export to your SIEM, and a short penetration checklist.
- Interop test: deploy AMI or container image (your choice) and verify start/stop lifecycle and model load times.

Attachments enclosed: networking-questions-table.xlsx (detailed fields we need filled), redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (test steps). We'll also attach the AMI provisioning guide if you elect that path.

Naomi
